items.informal_name: Composition of Divided Powers with Uniform Bell Scaling
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring A] {I : Ideal A} (self : DividedPowers I) {m n : ℕ} {x : A},
  n ≠ 0 → x ∈ I → self.dpow m (self.dpow n x) = ↑(m.uniformBell n) * self.dpow (m * n) x
items.informal_description: Let $ A $ be a commutative semiring and $ I $ an ideal of $ A $ equipped with a divided powers structure $ \gamma_n $. For natural numbers $ m, n $ with $ n \neq 0 $ and $ x \in I $, the composition $ \gamma_m(\gamma_n(x)) $ equals the product of the uniform Bell number $ \text{uniformBell}(m, n) $ and $ \gamma_{mn}(x) $. Formally, $ \gamma_m(\gamma_n(x)) = \text{uniformBell}(m, n) \cdot \gamma_{mn}(x) $.

items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring A] {I : Ideal A} [inst_1 : DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ I] {n : ℕ},
  IsUnit ↑(n - 1).factorial →
    I ^ n = 0 →
      ∀ {m k : ℕ},
        k ≠ 0 →
          ∀ {x : A},
            x ∈ I →
              DividedPowers.OfInvertibleFactorial.dpow I m (DividedPowers.OfInvertibleFactorial.dpow I k x) =
                ↑(m.uniformBell k) * DividedPowers.OfInvertibleFactorial.dpow I (m * k) x
items.informal_description: Under the conditions that $(n-1)!$ is invertible in $A$ and $I^n = 0$, for all natural numbers $m, k$ with $k \neq 0$ and $x \in I$, the composition of the divided power operations $\text{dpow}\, m$ and $\text{dpow}\, k$ applied to $x$ equals the product of the uniform Bell number $\text{uniformBell}(m, k)$ and the divided power operation $\text{dpow}\, (m \cdot k)$ applied to $x$.

items.informal_name: Composition of Divided Powers with Uniform Bell Number
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring A] {I : Ideal A} [inst_1 : DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ I] {n : ℕ},
  IsUnit ↑(n - 1).factorial →
    ∀ {m k : ℕ},
      k ≠ 0 →
        m * k < n →
          ∀ {x : A},
            x ∈ I →
              DividedPowers.OfInvertibleFactorial.dpow I m (DividedPowers.OfInvertibleFactorial.dpow I k x) =
                ↑(m.uniformBell k) * DividedPowers.OfInvertibleFactorial.dpow I (m * k) x
items.informal_description: For natural numbers $m, k$ (with $k \neq 0$) and an element $x$ in an ideal $I$ of a semiring $A$, if $(n-1)!$ is invertible in $A$ and $m \cdot k < n$, then the $m$-th divided power of the $k$-th divided power of $x$ equals the uniform Bell number $\text{uniformBell}(m, k)$ multiplied by the $(m \cdot k)$-th divided power of $x$. Formally, $\text{dpow}_I(m, \text{dpow}_I(k, x)) = \text{uniformBell}(m, k) \cdot \text{dpow}_I(m \cdot k, x)$.

items.informal_name: Coefficient-wise Derivation Acts on Polynomial Coefficients
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A]
  [inst_3 : AddCommGroup M] [inst_4 : Module A M] [inst_5 : Module R M] (d : Derivation R A M) (p : Polynomial A)
  (i : ℕ), (d.mapCoeffs p) i = d (p.coeff i)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p \in A[X] $ and index $ i \in \mathbb{N} $, the coefficient-wise derivation $ \text{mapCoeffs} $ satisfies $ (\text{mapCoeffs} \, p)(i) = d(\text{coeff}_i(p)) $, where $ d : A \to M $ is an $ R $-derivation and $ \text{coeff}_i(p) $ denotes the $ i $-th coefficient of $ p $. This establishes that the derivation acts on each polynomial coefficient individually while preserving the module structure and satisfying the Leibniz rule.

items.informal_name: Composition with A-Linear Map Induces Linear Map on Derivations
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {M : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring A]
  [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_3 : Algebra R A] [inst_4 : Module A M] [inst_5 : Module R M] {N : Type u_5}
  [inst_6 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_7 : Module A N] [inst_8 : Module R N] [inst_9 : IsScalarTower R A M]
  [inst_10 : IsScalarTower R A N] (f : M →ₗ[A] N), Derivation.llcomp f = f.compDer
items.informal_description: For any $ A $-linear map $ f : M 	o N $, the linear map from the space of derivations $ \mathrm{Derivation}(R, A, M) $ to $ \mathrm{Derivation}(R, A, N) $ induced by composing $ f $ with each derivation is equal to the composition of $ f $ with the derivation map.
